name: Parity Multisig Library Freeze
architecture: Shared, delegatecall-linked library contract backing hundreds of independently deployed Parity multisig wallets.
rootCause: The shared wallet library contract was deployed without being initialized. On 6 November 2017, a user (GitHub handle devops199) called initWallet on the uninitialized library, becoming its sole owner, then called its kill() function, self-destructing the library contract.
fundLockMechanism: Every wallet that delegatecall'd into the library depended on its bytecode for all wallet logic, including withdrawals. Once the library self-destructed, that bytecode no longer existed at its address, so every dependent wallet's withdrawal logic became permanently unreachable — a single library dependency bricking hundreds of otherwise-independent wallets at once.

amount.note: 513,774.16 ETH is the widely reported frozen amount; its USD value is commonly cited around $150M using November 2017 pricing, but ranges toward $280M+ in sources using later ETH prices. We report the ETH amount as the primary verified figure.

recoveryAttempts: EIP-999 proposed a hard fork to restore the destroyed library's code and unlock the wallets; it did not reach consensus and was not adopted. As of this writing the funds remain inaccessible on-chain.

primarySources.title: A major vulnerability has frozen hundreds of millions of dollars of Ethereum
Parity CEO is confident that $150M in frozen Ethereum isn't lost forever

limitations: USD valuation is sensitive to the ETH/USD price used and the date of conversion; different reputable outlets report figures from roughly $150M to $300M+ for the same 513,774 ETH. We treat the ETH-denominated amount as the verified fact and the USD figure as an approximation.
